request.rationale: The initial scientific distinction is whether direct-torque control is materially constrained by compiled dynamics and singularity exit, or whether the more consequential gap is learned coverage and two-second stabilization. This candidate-free measurement directly tests the former without conflating it with policy quality. Strong, configuration-dependent acceleration, persistent post-impulse motion, or poor singularity-exit authority would justify dynamics-aware control and identification before interpreting a learning result; regular fast response with feasible, well-conditioned target branches would redirect the next action toward training and radius/angle/hold-stratified policy evaluation. request.candidates_and_roles: No learned candidates exist. Working and best-known roles remain empty; M2 is a candidate-free physical characterization, not a policy artifact.
request.cumulative_resource_use: One completed measurement (M2) and one failed execution attempt (M1, implementation history only; no evidence or completed measurement). No training steps or learned candidates have been used.
request.current_goal_gap: No learned candidate has yet been trained or measured, so the gap to 98% official success is completely unquantified. The candidate-free evidence narrows the gap to end-to-end acquisition and regulation from the singular contractual reset across the full 6--20 cm radial distribution, with launch timing, action-induced overshoot, and hold interruptions still unresolved.
request.current_synthesis: Observed in completed M2: the compiled model has two enabled gear-5 actuators, 2 ms Euler physics, a 20 ms visible control interval, zero gravity, explicit 0.5 damping and 0.01 armature, and compiled link masses of about 0.099 kg and 0.052 kg. Dense generalized mass matrices are about 0.010--0.012 kg*m^2 on the shoulder and 0.0102 kg*m^2 on the elbow across the sampled configurations. The contractual reset has FK at 0.22 m and a rank-1 endpoint Jacobian with singular values 0.2417 and 0.0. On a 24-point grid spanning radii 0.06, 0.14, and 0.20 m and eight angles, every target had at least one joint-limit-feasible inverse branch; all 48 branch solutions were full-rank with condition numbers from 1.67 to 5.29, although two individual branch solutions were joint-limit-infeasible. A one-control-interval unit action from reset or representative IK states generated roughly 5.5--6.1 rad/s peak joint speed and up to 4.4 cm endpoint displacement over the subsequent one-second open-loop response, while zero-torque velocity decayed to numerical zero by the final sample. Interpretation: the mechanism is not statically unreachable and has substantial direct-torque authority plus damping, but a one-interval command can move farther than the 1 cm hold ball, making velocity shaping and early capture plausible bottlenecks. Competing explanations remain: (A) a learned policy will mainly fail because the singular launch and direct-torque transient delay or overshoot first reach; (B) the dominant gap will be the visible training exposure mismatch, especially the omitted 6--14 cm inner annulus; (C) first reach will be adequate but residual endpoint motion will interrupt the 100-step hold. M2 supports the physical premises behind A and weakens static-feasibility and unknown-compiled-default explanations, but it does not test a policy, target-conditioned launch, closed-loop settling, runtime fidelity, or official protected semantics. The unit-action response is open-loop and cannot establish task success or causal failure attribution.
request.decision_frontier: The unresolved scientific distinction is whether the first end-to-end learning gap is (A) singularity-exit/torque-transient control, (B) coverage of the official inner radial annulus, or (C) local low-velocity stabilization for the uninterrupted hold. The discriminating evidence is a complete candidate artifact measured from the contractual reset on a radius- and angle-stratified development panel, preserving first-reach step, minimum/final distance, endpoint velocity or hold interruptions, maximum held steps, elbow branch, and action saturation. Outcomes concentrated in late first reach or large early excursions would favor a launch/trajectory intervention; comparable reach but short or interrupted holds would favor stabilization; failures concentrated at 6--14 cm would favor changing training exposure. Aggregate reward or minimum distance alone would not discriminate these alternatives.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal requires a learned policy to complete the full uninterrupted 2-second, 1 cm hold in at least 196 of 200 official episodes. M2 supplies the physical context needed to choose a learning experiment without mistaking static reachability or compiled defaults for demonstrated task success.
request.next_direction_or_closure: End startup with the candidate-free physical fork narrowed and move to goal review. The next credible direction is an end-to-end policy experiment—fresh training under an explicitly chosen exposure followed by matched radius/angle/hold diagnostics—because the current evidence shows enough actuation and branch feasibility to make policy behavior the next missing causal layer.
request.next_question: At goal review, decide whether to open a bounded inquiry testing end-to-end policy capability from the contractual singular reset across the full official radial range, with failure-class diagnostics separating launch/overshoot, inner-annulus coverage, and uninterrupted-hold stabilization.
